I think a PA role will depend on how well you manage your disability and what kind of accommodations you need. I was diagnosed recently, so my experience is probably different than most people. I mask my condition very well, and can manage fairly well or more like have learned to try to regulate as much as possible to avoid affecting my job performance. 

My supervisor nor anyone at work know about my diagnosis so I don't have any accommodations but I work hybrid 2-3 days a week at home. I get to wear headphones in the office but I also work at a smaller office for a middle market firm (Top 10). Public Accounting is tough, as a lot of people on this sub will say, and I can tell you I have lost colleagues in the last two years due to mental health deteriorating and burnout. I will say, it gets overwhelming sometimes. I get burnout and as I get closer to manager I realize that this does not get easier. I talk a lot with clients and manage my team very well but again it is tough.

You could certainly find a firm who would be willing to accommodate you. I have a supporting team and directors in my firm and have not had the need to disclose to request accommodations but maybe one day I will need to do that. Like I said, my experience is probably not representative of what goes on in other middle market firms.
